sources.title: Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain
sources.finding: Adult female brain: 139,255 neurons, 54.5 million synaptic contacts. Connectivity is structural; no recorded activity is bundled.
sources.release: v783; October 2023 segmentation snapshot, with later public annotation updates

sources.title: Whole-brain annotation and multi-connectome cell typing of Drosophila
sources.finding: Companion annotation resource for FlyWire; cell typing and cross-connectome comparisons require specimen-specific identifiers.

sources.title: Distributed control circuits across a brain-and-cord connectome
sources.authors: Bates, Phelps, Kim, Yang et al.
sources.finding: Adult female brain and nerve cord. Published figure reports 155,916 proofread/roughly proofread neurons. Local sensory-effector loops are linked by longer pathways.
sources.limits: Lamina, ocelli and ocellar ganglion missing. 171,512 accounted-for objects includes fragments/glia/trachea. Do not label all objects neurons or compare unqualified predicted-synapse totals.
sources.release: v888 publication dataset; v2 synapse snapshot used in paper; v3 also available

sources.title: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
sources.finding: 166,700 annotated neurons: 166,483 connected plus 217 without synapses. The proofread graph has 124.2 million synaptic connections and approximately 25.58 million directed edges.
sources.limits: Synapses are predictions, not individually proofread. Missing lamina/ocellar tissue. Distinct male specimen; IDs cannot substitute for FlyWire roots.

sources.title: The organization of visual pathways in the Drosophila brain
sources.finding: MaleCNS analysis maps parallel visual pathways beyond the optic lobes and predicts receptive-field structure; network predictions are compared with physiology.
sources.limits: Structural predictions do not provide recorded activity for every cell.

sources.title: The connectome of an insect brain
sources.finding: Larval brain reconstruction comprises 3,016 neurons and approximately 548,000 synapses, with extensive recurrent connectivity.
sources.limits: Specific distributed matrices contain filtered subsets and compartment channels; their node counts need not equal the paper's full reconstruction count.

sources.title: Dragonfly target-detecting neurons adapt to stimulus saliency
sources.finding: Small-target neurons show saliency-dependent adaptation. Contrast, preferred direction and target jitter affect adaptation.
sources.limits: Data available on request; no whole-dragonfly connectome or downloadable neural morphology is supplied by this paper.

sources.title: Neuronal segmentation in cephalopod arms
sources.finding: Octopus axial nerve cords contain repeated neuronal segments and a topographic organization associated with suckers.
sources.limits: Anatomical modules are not a whole-octopus synapse-level connectome.
sources.articleLicense: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; verify separate asset licenses before adapting imagery

sources.title: Multiple Longitudinal Tracts in the Cephalopod Arm Sensorimotor System
sources.finding: Distinct longitudinal tracts in octopus arm neuropil and cerebrobrachial pathways suggest anatomical substrates for coordinating movements along an arm.
sources.limits: Not synapse-level connectivity or a validated arm-control simulation.
